facility.name: Childrens Corner First Presbyterian
facility.programs_provided: School Age Care,Meals Provided ,Snacks Provided,Part Time Care,Field Trips

provenance.note: Census Geocoder Exact match: 800 JEFFERSON ST, KERRVILLE, TX, 78028

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: The training certificate that was provided did not meet the requirements for first aid certification.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Caregivers were observed in the classroom closet with their back to the children and engaged in setting up nap mats while children were eating lunch with a child in the classroom with food intolerances.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: During the investigation, it was found that a staff member did not have a current first aid certification.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Tables and Chairs Safe, Easy to Clean and Appropriate in Size: During the course of the investigation, it was observed that a child wearing an oversized tshirt had the shirt pulled over the back of the chair they were sitting on to keep them secured in the seat.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Tables and Chairs Safe, Easy to Clean and Appropriate in Size (26 TAC §746.4501(a))

occurrences.finding: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Injuries Requiring Medical Treatment or Hospitalization: The operation failed to complete an incident report after a child received an injury while in care that required medical attention.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Licensing Incident/Illness Report Form - Injuries Requiring Medical Treatment or Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.701(1))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Safety Documentation for Emergency Drills, Fire Extinguishers, & Smoke Detectors: Emergency drills have not been documented for 2026.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Safety Documentation for Emergency Drills, Fire Extinguishers, & Smoke Detectors (26 TAC §746.801(10))

occurrences.finding: Safety-Hinged Lid Storage Containers Safe: There was a black storage container on the larger playground with a lid that was not secured to prevent accidental closure.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Bodies of Water Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3701(8))

occurrences.finding: Written Operational Policies - Emergency Preparedness Plans: Upon review of the operation's emergency preparedness plan it was missing information on how children who were non-mobile will be evacuated, the evacuation location if children and staff can not return to the operation, and how continuity of care will be maintained at the relocation site.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Operational Policies - Emergency Preparedness Plans (26 TAC §746.501(a)(24))

occurrences.finding: Administering Medication - Original Container with Child's Name, Date: Two medictions stored at the operation did not contain the original prescription for the medication.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Administering Medication - Original Container with Child's Name, Date (26 TAC §746.3805(b)(1))

occurrences.finding: Medication No Longer Used: An over the counter medication kept at the operation for a child enrolled expired 11/2024.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Medication No Longer Used (26 TAC §746.3809)

occurrences.finding: Posting of Activity Plan: Two classrooms did not have current activity plans posted.  The last posted plan was dated 8/5.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Posting of Activity Plan (26 TAC §746.2209)

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pre-Service Training: One out of ten staff training files evaluated did not have documentation that a caregiver without 2 yrs prior work experience completed the first 8 hours of pre-service training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pre-Service Training (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(2)(A))

occurrences.finding: Documentation of Fire Inspection: The most recent fire inspection report was not available for inspection.  The last recorded inspection was held 8/15/23.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documentation of Fire Inspection (26 TAC §746.5103)

occurrences.finding: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries: The operation failed to provide a incident report or information regarding an injury a child received while in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries (26 TAC §746.307(c))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: The slide on the climbing unit continues to be roped off and has not been repaired or replaced.  Exposed tree roots have not been removed or covered from the playground.    NOTE:  This is a recite.  Documentation was provided that the operation is in the process of purchasing a replacement slide with the playground vendor.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Safety - Televisions Anchored to Prevent Tip Over: A television in the dramatic play area was at the children's level and not anchored to avoid possibly being pulled down off the shelf.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Televisions Anchored to Prevent Tip Over (26 TAC §746.3701(10))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: The slide on the climbing unit is currently taped off at the top and bottom of the slide.  The bottom of the slide has two broken areas where children can be injured or clothing could potentially get caught on.  There are also numerous tree roots exposed on the larger playground that can cause a tripping hazard.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Documentation of Annual Sanitation Inspection: The operation did not have a current sanitation inspection available for review.  The last recorded inspection was conducted on 1/10/23.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documentation of Annual Sanitation Inspection (26 TAC §746.3403)

occurrences.finding: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games: A caregiver was observed using their personal tablet while supervising children during nap time.    NOTE:   Caregiver put tablet away during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Personal use of electronic devices, such as cell phones, MP3 players, tablets, and video games (26 TAC §746.1203(3)(D))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: 2 out of 10 staff did not have a current 1st Aid certificate on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: A caregivers purse was out on the floor next to a sleeping child.    NOTE:  The caregiver placed their purse in a cabinet during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training- Required Content: 7 out of 10 caregivers had not completed training in the following topics for the anniversary years evaluated:  emergency preparedness; preventing and controlling the spread of communicable diseases, including immunizations (this requirement was previously an optional topic); administering medication; preventing and responding to emergencies due to food or an allergic reaction; building and physical premises safety; and handling, storing, and disposing of hazardous materials.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training- Required Content (26 TAC §746.1309(e))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR: 2 out of 10 caregivers did not have a current CPR certificate on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR (26 TAC §746.1315(b))

occurrences.finding: Health Statement parent sign - Dated within past yr, name/address health care professional, states child can participate. Follow by signed statement: 1 out of 2 missing health statements had not been obtained containing  a doctor signature after the child had been in attendance for 12 months.    Note:  This is a recite.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Health Statement parent sign - Dated within past yr, name/address health care professional, states child can participate. Follow by signed statement (26 TAC §746.611(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Health Statement parent sign - Dated within past yr, name/address health care professional, states child can participate. Follow by signed statement: 2 out of 10 child files evaluated did not have a health statement signed by a doctor after being in attendance for 12 months.    Note:  This is a recite.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Health Statement parent sign - Dated within past yr, name/address health care professional, states child can participate. Follow by signed statement (26 TAC §746.611(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Nutrition and Food Service - Follow Meal Patterns: The operation ordered takeout food to serve the children for lunch when the cook was absent and did not include additional food components in order to follow the USDA meal patterns.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Nutrition and Food Service - Follow Meal Patterns (26 TAC §746.3301(b))

occurrences.finding: Daily Menus - Record Comparable Substitutions: The operation did not keep record of food substitutions to their weekly planned menus.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Daily Menus - Record Comparable Substitutions (26 TAC §746.3313(1))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: A church member had direct access to children ages 13-16 months of age without an eligibility letter on file.    NOTE: A background check was submitted through the operation's portal during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Health Statement parent sign - Dated within past yr, name/address health care professional, states child can participate. Follow by signed statement: 2 out of 10 child files evaluated did not have a health statement signed by a doctor after being in attendance for 12 months.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Health Statement parent sign - Dated within past yr, name/address health care professional, states child can participate. Follow by signed statement (26 TAC §746.611(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current: 1 out of 10 child files evaluated was missing updated vaccination records for a child who was 16 mos of age.  The child was missing their MMR & Varicella vaccinations.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current (26 TAC §746.613(b))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: The operation failed to notify Licensing that a child was potentially placed at risk of injury when bleach water was accidentally sprayed on the child's hair.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: Cleaning bottles were not properly labeled with the contents contained and as a result, bleach water was sprayed on a child's hair.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Incident/Illness Report Form Signed: The incident report was not signed by a management person at the operation until 7 days after the incident report was completed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Incident/Illness Report Form Signed (26 TAC §746.705)

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: 3 out 10 child files reviewed for immunization records were missing updated immunizations.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: A caregiver in the infant room was present and  in direct care of the children without an eligibility letter on file.      NOTE:  The caregiver was removed from the operation and a background check will be submitted by the director.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: AP Cribs - Only Snug Fitting Sheet and Crib Mattress Cover Allowed if Infant Younger than 12 Months of Age: An infant, 8 months of age, was observed sleeping in their crib with a blanket.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Cribs - Only Snug Fitting Sheet and Crib Mattress Cover Allowed if Infant Younger than 12 Months of Age (26 TAC §746.2415(b))

occurrences.finding: Infant May Not Sleep in a Restrictive Device: Two infants were observed sleeping in a swing.  When caregivers were asked how long the infants had been sleeping in the swings, it was said to be 10 minutes.    NOTE:  Caregivers moved the children to their assigned cribs.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant May Not Sleep in a Restrictive Device (26 TAC §746.2426)

occurrences.finding: Adequate Lighting During Naptime: Two Prek classrooms were observed not having adequate lighting to allow caregivers to see the children while sleeping from the opposite side of the room.    NOTE:  Caregivers opened a window blind to allow natural light to come into the room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Adequate Lighting During Naptime (26 TAC §746.2911)

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: A caregiver in the infant room was present and  in direct care of the children without an eligibility letter on file.      NOTE:  The caregiver was removed from the operation and a background check will be submitted by the director.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries: The operation did not notify a parent that their child received a minor injury received while in care during naptime.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries (26 TAC §746.307(c))

occurrences.finding: Required Health Statement - Written, dated within past year, indicates child is physically able to participate in operation's child-care program: Two out of ten child files evaluated were missing a health statement from a physician after being in attendance for 12 months.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Health Statement - Written, dated within past year, indicates child is physically able to participate in operation's child-care program (26 TAC §746.611(a)(1))
